conviction_note: The quarter was pre-guided on 16 Sep to the high end of NII +4-6% and fees +12-14% ('maybe even above'), and consensus (NII +6.2%, fees +14.1%, revenue $7.99-8.01B, EPS $1.32) already sits at that high end, so the reported quarter carries little. What is left is the Q3 rate shock: the 10y rose about 85bp in the quarter. That cuts two ways, a steeper repricing tailwind for the Q4/2027 NII guide against AOCI drag on the buyback restart and WFC-style commercial deposit-cost pressure. The pieces roughly offset (impact_sum -0.1). p_up sits at 48, a hair under 50, because USB fell on 6 of its last 7 prints, including two beat-and-raise quarters. abs_move is 2.8, slightly under the 3.15 implied move because the quarter was pre-released mid-quarter, so the scaled number is about -0.1. Both measurements say: no edge.
bar: Revenue ~$7.99-8.01B and EPS $1.32 (Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/usb/earnings and Zacks via AAII https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/515597-what-you-need-to-know-about-us-bancorps-q3-earnings agree on $1.32; Zacks NII +6.2% y/y, fees +14.1% y/y). Company guide: Q3 revenue $7.876-8.023B (Q2 2026 deck, https://www.webull.com/news/15237865861178368), updated 2026-09-16 to the high end of NII +4-6% and fees +12-14% (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/us-bancorp-at-barclays-conference-fee-growth-and-margin-gains-93CH-4904020). On the Q3 2025 base (NII TE ~$4.25B, fees ~$3.08B, https://finviz.com/news/195164/us-bancorp-stock-gains-as-q3-earnings-beat-on-nii-fee-income-growth), the high end is ~$8.02B, so consensus sits at the top of the guide.
positioning_check: Short interest was 24.8M shares, 3.4 days to cover (FINRA settlement 2026-07-15 via https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/usb/short-interest/), about 1.6% of ~1.56B shares, so the short is not crowded. 25d skew is -0.83 vol points (calls marginally richer), put/call OI 0.74, and the baseline reads the priced lean as balanced. The stock is -6.24% over 20d and -14.4% from its 52w high, and has fallen from $61.21 on 2026-09-16 to $56.00. Several targets were cut into the print: Evercore to $65 on 10-01, Truist $69->$67 on 10-01, Raymond James $74->$72 on 10-06.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-16 the CFO guided Q3 NII to the high end of +4-6% y/y and fees to the high end of +12-14% 'and maybe even above'. Since then, Q3 peer prints on 2026-10-13 showed strong equities trading (GS) and investment banking (Citi), which supports the BTIG-driven part of the fee beat. JPM's FICC slowdown cuts against USB's legacy debt-capital-markets fees. Merchant processing was guided flat y/y and is inside the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat ($1.35 vs $1.27) with a raised outlook bought +1.59%. Q3 2025 also beat on NII and fees and fell -1.72%. The stock fell on 6 of 7 prints in the baseline, so beats are mostly sold.
findings.why_not_priced: The high-end guide itself is priced: consensus NII +6.2% and fees +14.1% already sit on it. The only unpriced piece is the 'maybe above' on fees, which consensus at exactly +14.1% does not carry. If the market had priced it, revenue consensus would be above the $8.02B high end of the range, and it is not ($7.99-8.01B).
findings.independence: GS equities-led beat and Citi IB strength, 2026-10-13 (https://fortune.com/2026/10/13/jpmorgan-goldman-sachs-citigroup-wells-fargo-interest-inflation/). That is a peer proxy and only partly independent: JPM missed on FICC in the same source, which points the other way for legacy capital markets.

findings.finding: The 10y Treasury rose about 85bp in Q3 2026, from ~4.42% on 06-30 to ~5.1-5.2% in late September. USB reported CET1 of 9.4% including AOCI at June 30 against a 10% Category II target, with Category II 'second or third quarter' and buybacks paused in Q3. AOCI drag is therefore a risk to the size or timing of the promised buyback restart.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to a capital-return surprise in the baseline. The Q2 2026 print, when the CFO flagged buybacks held at $200M, bought +1.59%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: yields are public, and the stock has fallen ~8.5% since 09-16 alongside them. The residual is the move after the CFO spoke. The 10y was ~5.01% on 09-14 (https://www.mortgagenewsdaily.com:443/treasury) when he said 'we expect to go back right into share purchases and to increase those'. It reached ~5.11% on 09-23 and higher by quarter end, so the AOCI-inclusive ratio at 09-30 is worse than what he was looking at. A fully priced version would show consensus cutting the Q4 buyback, and no source shows that.
findings.independence: The CET1 9.4%-incl-AOCI figure comes from the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/07/23/us-bancorp-usb-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). The AOCI-to-buyback link is my inference, not confirmed by the company: a macro-to-company proxy, sized small.

findings.finding: Q3 brought mild steepening, with the 10y up ~85bp against the 2y up ~75bp. The CFO said on the Q2 call that 'the hikes in and of themselves are not consequential. It's more, what's the shape of the curve after that?', and on 09-16 reaffirmed a path to a 3% NIM next year with NII and NIM growing in Q3 and Q4. Higher long rates speed up fixed-asset repricing, which supports the Q4/2027 NII guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 raised outlook bought +1.59%. The Q1 2026 print fell -1.58%, and that reaction has no line attribution in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The 3% NIM target is public. What is new is that the long end moved more after the target was set. If the market had priced a better 2027 NII trajectory, USB would not have lagged as yields rose (-8.5% since 09-16) and targets would not have been cut into the print.
findings.independence: The quarterly yield moves come from a separate source (https://stockhub.kr/en/news/news_6701ef10d8c8). Caveat already netted into the size: the curve flattened in late September (10y-2y ~26bp on 09-23 against ~36bp on 09-14), so the steepening is modest.

findings.finding: Wells Fargo's Q3 2026 release, out 2026-10-13 after USB last spoke, showed NII up only 5% y/y with gains partly offset by higher deposit costs on interest-bearing commercial deposits after the September hike. The stock fell 1.5-3% on a revenue disappointment. That is a read-through risk to USB's deposit costs and its Q4 NII guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history on USB. Peer WFC sold off 1.5-3% on an NII and revenue disappointment the same week.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a peer print landing after USB's last guidance (09-16). USB's NII consensus of +6.2% sits at the top of its range and leaves no room for a deposit-cost drag. If the market had priced it, USB's NII consensus would sit mid-range (~+5%), not at the top.
findings.independence: Market reaction: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/13/goldman-sachs-rises-on-equities-led-earnings-beat-jpmorgan-chase-treads-water-wells-fargo-declines-3/. JPM's NII ex-Markets was +6%, so the peer read is mixed. USB said on the Q2 call that deposit rates rose only 'a couple of basis points' and depend on loan growth.

findings.finding: Into a quarter whose guide management firmed upward on 09-16, the stock has fallen ~8.5% (from $61.21 to $56.00) and three brokers cut targets (Evercore to $65, Truist to $67, Raymond James to $72). Expectations for the stock fell while the quarter's guide rose.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last eight-quarter pattern is 1 of 7 up. The one up print (Q2 2026, +1.59%) came after a beat-and-raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The drawdown has a visible cause, sector rotation and rising yields (https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-us-bancorp-stock-sliding-today-93CH-5595490), and that cause can keep running. Only a sliver is a lowered bar, and the balanced skew and the sells-beats history keep it small.

baseline_tension: Neither cuts against the baseline: the skew is balanced and the evidence nets to roughly zero. The -6.24% run-up came from yields and sector rotation, the same macro that drives the two offsetting rate findings, so it is largely priced.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): finding 1 cut from +0.3 to +0.2 because consensus already sits at the high end of the guided ranges; only the 'maybe above' on fees is outside it

Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission): AOCI/buyback finding cut from -0.4 to -0.3 because the company had already spoken after most of the yield move; steepening finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2 because the curve flattened in late September
Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): p_up moved from 50 to 48, since the stock fell on 6 of 7 prints including beat-and-raise quarters

Rule 7 / positioning: added a small +0.1 positioning finding (expectations lowered into a firmed guide) that was not in the draft; short interest checked (3.4 days, not crowded), which leaves the negatives unshrunk
WFC peer read-through (-0.3) left standing: a peer print after the company last spoke is the pattern the file says has worked, sized small as a proxy
